narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 79.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That is a high-risk prediction: it does not prove you cannot succeed, but it was strong enough for the school to deny admission at this time.

The strongest factor was your year-three class standing. You are in the first decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile, and this low standing pushed the prediction toward failure. Your year-one standing was the second most important factor; it was also first decile versus an accepted average near the sixth, adding further risk. The third factor, your upper-middle family-income background, worked in the opposite direction—it slightly favored passing and is common among accepted students—but it was not enough to offset the academic indicators.

To move forward, ask admissions for feedback and whether an appeal or reapplication is possible. If you reapply, focus on strengthening the weakest academic signals, consider retaking the LSAT if feasible, and provide context for your early academic record. Seek pre-law or admissions advising to build a realistic plan.
